clue.text: Old flier ordered removal of these hundred wines

definitions.text: Old flier ordered removal of these

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
hock is a German white wine, so wines gives the plural

explanation.surface: A veteran airman orders a hundred bottles of wine taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: Old wartime pilots called 'Chocks away!' to have the wedges removed from the wheels before take-off; that is the definition. HOCK is the British name for Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The wooden wedges holding an aircraft's wheels were pulled away on the pilot's command before take-off.

clue.text: Principal variety of each complaint

parts.note: the head is the principal of a school

indicators.note: a different arrangement of the letters of the word each

explanation.surface: The headmaster lists every kind of grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense, a pain in the head being a common ailment.

clue.text: Savage — can bite a little, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the words are taken by how they are spoken

parts.note: is able to nibble, which spoken runs together

explanation.surface: Warning about a fierce creature that may take a small bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' says CAN NIBBLE, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eater, the archetypal wild person of old adventure stories.

clue.text: Set up records to conclude our magnificent show

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised upward means read from bottom to top

parts.note: LPs are long-playing records
to end

explanation.surface: Records are assembled for the finale of a grand performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour is grandeur or a magnificent display.

clue.text: Aid near? Dodo, alas, is unfortunately past it

indicators.note: signals the letters of the preceding words are in a sorry, disordered state

explanation.surface: A lament over the extinct dodo, beyond all aid.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means utterly lifeless or finished, beyond revival.

clue.text: A minor gap in privacy from the butler's eye?

definitions.text: A minor gap in privacy from the butler's eye?

parts.words: A minor gap in privacy from the butler's eye?
parts.note: the small opening in a door through which a nosy servant might peep

explanation.surface: A servant's snooping eye intrudes slightly on the family's privacy.
explanation.definitionFit: The small opening in a lock that an eavesdropping servant traditionally peers through.

clue.text: He's tested an explosive device in a river

indicators.note: the device is placed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
a mine, with the article before it

explanation.surface: A bomb-disposal expert checks a mine found in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate sitting a test is one who is examined.

clue.text: "A sweet —— in the dress" (Herrick)

parts.note: the opening line of Robert Herrick's poem praising untidiness in clothing, with the missing word left as a blank

explanation.surface: A line of seventeenth-century verse about a charmingly untidy dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Herrick's poem celebrates artful untidiness, a lack of neat order in attire.

clue.text: Mississippi flower-tree

parts.note: the American state of Mississippi has the same blossoming tree as both its state flower and its state tree, and is nicknamed after it

explanation.surface: A botanical label for the emblem of a southern US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Mississippi is known as the Magnolia State, its official flower and tree being this large-blossomed plant.

clue.text: Roundabout way for 7 to succeed ?

definitions.meaning: a road that goes round a town rather than through it
the candidate at 7 down succeeds by means of a pass in the test

explanation.surface: A road-planning note about how a candidate might get through.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring road is a detour avoiding a centre; split in two, the phrase says a candidate wins through by passing the exam.

clue.text: A French company put in hand rearrangement of Spanish estate

indicators.note: the article and company are placed inside the reworked letters of the following word
signals that the letters of the word hand are to be reordered

parts.note: Cie is the French abbreviation for compagnie, company

explanation.surface: A French firm takes over and reorganises a Spanish ranch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearrangement of' reorders the letters of 'hand', and 'put in' places the French article and company inside them; Cie is the French short form for a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a large landed estate or ranch in Spain or Latin America.

clue.text: Shopkeeper a minor pro, prophet? That's right

clue.text: Worshipful old Indian state returned to the French

indicators.note: sent back, so the name of the state is read from right to left

parts.note: Baroda was a princely state of India, now Vadodara
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A former Indian state handed back to France, described reverently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns the state's name backwards. Baroda was one of the princely states of British India, a convention a modern solver may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worshipful deserves adoration, the sense of the adjective here.

clue.text: Unhurriedly making a garland, no doubt

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian flower garland
surely, certainly

explanation.surface: Someone takes their time weaving a garland, without question.
explanation.definitionFit: Done slowly and without haste, at one's ease.

clue.text: Circus performer's stamp of authority

definitions.meaning: a marine mammal trained to balance balls in a circus ring
an official impression in wax confirming a document

explanation.surface: A circus act gets official approval.
explanation.definitionFit: The performing marine animal and the official mark of approval share one word.

clue.text: How to sit a horse, right up in the saddle

indicators.note: the reversed abbreviation goes inside the word for the seat
in a down clue, read upwards, from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Riding advice: sit upright in the saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the abbreviation backwards because this is a down light, and 'in' sets it just after the first letter of the seat word.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit astride, a leg on each side, is the way a rider sits on a horse.

clue.text: Warn Scottish advertiser over his difficulty?

parts.note: an ad man, with mon the Scots pronunciation of man

indicators.note: the word his is in difficulty, its letters muddled

explanation.surface: Cautioning a Scots advertising man about his problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficulty?' jumbles 'his', and 'over' joins the pieces in the down light. 'Mon' is a stage-Scots spelling of man, so a Scottish ad man is an ad mon.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprove or caution someone firmly.

clue.text: Clothing motorists get into

definitions.meaning: kit or garments, as in sports clothes
drivers select first, second and so on on the gearbox

explanation.surface: Drivers pulling on their outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, clothes are kit; drivers also engage a cog ratio, the same word.

clue.text: Jokes about the French lady doctor in evening dress

indicators.note: the jokes go round the outside of the remaining pieces

parts.note: gags are jokes
la is the feminine French for the

explanation.surface: A female doctor in a ballgown is the butt of jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the jokes round the rest; 'the French lady' gives the feminine article, not a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags is slang for one's best clothes, worn for an evening out.

clue.text: Article in paper is changed in value

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: signals the letters of the words that come before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: An article in a newspaper has been revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges the letters of 'paper is'; 'in' is only a link, and the article opens the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To appraise is to assess the worth of something.

clue.text: Knights, though errant, should not lose these bearings

definitions.text: Knights, though errant, should not lose these bearings

parts.words: Knights, though errant, should not lose these bearings
parts.note: bearings here are the heraldic devices on a knight's shield, not a sense of direction a wandering knight might lose

explanation.surface: Advice that wandering knights should keep their sense of direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldic devices on a shield are called arms, and the adjective describing them is the word for coats of arms.

clue.text: Does this eclipse make invalid artist upset?

parts.note: annul means cancel or declare void

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Would this eclipse cancel the painter's work?
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-shaped eclipse, where the moon leaves a bright circle of sun visible.

clue.text: How much for a horse?

definitions.meaning: the total or quantity asked about
a mount is a horse for riding, with the article in front

explanation.surface: Someone asking the price of a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A total quantity; read as two words it is an article followed by a riding animal.

clue.text: Versatile players lose all in this game

indicators.note: the versatile players drop a part of their name, the word given next

parts.note: all-rounders are cricketers who both bat and bowl well

explanation.surface: Even talented players can lose everything in this sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose' takes ALL from ALLROUNDERS. ROUNDERS is a British bat-and-ball game like baseball, played in schools.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional British bat-and-ball game played by schoolchildren, ancestor of baseball.

clue.text: Recognized procedures for bores

definitions.meaning: routines everyone knows, such as a fire practice
boring tools used to make holes

explanation.surface: Tedious people following set routines.
explanation.definitionFit: Set routines practised by rote, and also tools for boring holes.

clue.text: A day of triumph with many a song or prayer

parts.note: VE Day, Victory in Europe Day, 8 May 1945
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: A victorious day celebrated with singing and prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: VE Day marked the Allied victory in Europe in 1945.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin Hail Mary, a Catholic devotion addressed to the Virgin.

clue.text: Heavenly piece of cake — the real thing

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is taken, a run running across them

explanation.surface: A slice of cake so good it is divine, the genuine article.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across caKE THE REAL; 'piece of' looks like part of the idiom 'piece of cake'.
explanation.definitionFit: Celestial or airy and otherworldly, as heaven is.

clue.text: Agreeable fellows

parts.note: agreeable read literally: men who always agree with the boss rather than pleasant company

explanation.surface: A description of pleasant chaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Sycophants who always say the affirmative word to a superior.
